bottom_line: Compared with placebo, apixaban 10 mg once daily increased ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.45; 95% confidence interval, 1.31 to 4.61; P⫽0.005).
implications: In this phase 2 trial, adding apixaban to antiplatelet therapy increased ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding versus placebo (eg, HR 2.45 [95% CI, 1.31 to 4.61] for 10 mg once daily), while ischemic outcomes were numerically lower but not statistically significant in the reported lower-dose arms (eg, HR 0.61 [95% CI, 0.35 to 1.04]). The discontinuation of the 2 higher-dose arms for excess bleeding indicates higher doses had unacceptable bleeding in this setting, and the results do not establish a definitive efficacy benefit on ischemic events.

major_points.text: Phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial in recent ACS patients.
major_points.quote:
Apixaban for Prevention of Acute Ischemic and Safety Events (APPRAISE) was a phase 2,
  double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study.

major_points.text: Randomized 1715 patients to placebo or 4 apixaban dosing regimens for 6 months.
major_points.quote:
Patients (n⫽1715) with recent ST-elevation or non–ST-elevation
  acute coronary syndrome were randomized to 6 months of placebo (n⫽611) or 1 of 4 doses of apixaban

major_points.text: Most patients received aspirin and many received clopidogrel.
major_points.quote:
Nearly all patients
  received aspirin; 76% received clopidogrel.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.
major_points.quote:
The primary outcome was International Society of Thrombosis and
  Hemostasis major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.

major_points.text: Two higher-dose apixaban arms were discontinued due to excess total bleeding.
major_points.quote:
At the recommendation of the Data Monitoring Committee, the
  2 higher-dose apixaban arms were discontinued because of excess total bleeding.

major_points.text: Apixaban increased bleeding in a dose-dependent fashion versus placebo for the lower-dose arms reported.
major_points.quote:
Compared with placebo, apixaban 2.5
  mg twice daily (hazard ratio, 1.78; 95% confidence interval, 0.91 to 3.48; P⫽0.09) and 10 mg once daily (hazard ratio,
  2.45; 95% confidence interval, 1.31 to 4.61; P⫽0.005)

major_points.text: Ischemic events were numerically lower with apixaban versus placebo in the two lower-dose arms reported.
Bleeding increase was more pronounced and ischemic reduction less evident with background aspirin plus clopidogrel compared with aspirin alone.
major_points.quote:
The increase in bleeding was more pronounced and the reduction in
  ischemic events was less evident in patients taking aspirin plus clopidogrel than in those taking aspirin alone.
